items.title: Retrieval-augmented generation
items.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a technique that enables large language models (LLMs) to retrieve and incorporate new information from external data sources. With RAG, LLMs first refer to a specified set of documents, then respond to user queries. These documents supplement information from the LLM's pre-existing training data. This allows LLMs to use domain-specific and/or updated information that is not available in the training data. For example, this enables LLM-based chatbots to access internal company data or generate responses based on authoritative sources. The technique was first proposed in 2020 and has since become a widely adopted approach in modern AI systems.

In 2021, a group of employees at OpenAI left to start a new company focused on the safe development of artificial intelligence. items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary: Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] “Robots are advancing quickly, but developing them for real-world environments remains slow, data-intensive and difficult to scale,” Huang said. “Working with UC Berkeley, NVIDIA is helping advance a new approach combining agentic AI, simulation and open industrial task-focused benchmarks to help developers rapidly test and improve robot behavior before deployment.” [...] Earlier this year, he and his team began experimenting with a change to the way the robot code is organized. Using a framework they called Graph-as-Policy, robot tasks are segmented into individual skills, such as finding an object, planning a grasp and moving the gripper without collisions. Goldberg likened it to individual building blocks that fit together into something much larger.

items.title: 同一张价目表，算不出一次任务的账
items.summary:
同一张价目表，算不出一次任务的账

11 月 10 日我把 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的官方价目表对着看了一遍。标准短上下文，每百万 token 的输入价和输出价，gpt-6-astra 是 10 美元和 50 美元，gpt-6.1-sol 是 2 美元和 10 美元，gpt-6.1-terra 是 1 美元和 5 美元，gpt-6-luna 是 0.10 美元和 0.50 美元。Anthropic 这边，Claude Fable 5.1 是 10 美元和 50 美元，Opus 5.5 是 4 美元和 20 美元，Sonnet 5.5 是 2 美元和 10 美元，Haiku 5.5 在提示不超过十万 token 时是 0.10 美元和 0.50 美元。

高、中、低三档摆在一起，Claude 和 GPT 在同档上已经给出同样的数字。两家的批量档都大约是标准价的一半。价目表看上去站到了同一条线上，低价档已经压到每百万 0.10 美元和 0.50 美元。

可价目表也会往上走。谷歌给 Gemini 4 Argon 的导入价是每百万 2 美元和 10 美元，用到 11 月 30 日，12 月 1 日起标准价变成 4 美元和 20 美元。Anthropic 的 Sonnet 5 上市时挂过 2 美元和 10 美元的导入价，截至 8 月 31 日，后来这个价格成了标准价，原定 9 月 1 日调到 3 美元和 15 美元的计划取消了。一家结束了导入价，一家把导入价改成了标准价。看单一档位的单价，很容易把这种来回当成单向降价。

上下文长度很容易把单价抬上去。OpenAI 的输入超过 27.2 万 token 会走更高的长上下文价格，sol 从 2 美元和 10 美元变成 4 美元和 15 美元。Anthropic 的 Haiku 5.5 在提示超过十万 token 后，从 0.10 美元和 0.50 美元跳到 0.50 美元和 2.50 美元，输入价翻了五倍。同一款模型，长文档和短问答可以按两套价格结算。

服务档位也会改变单价。批量档约为标准价一半，加速档约为标准价两倍。12 小时缓存写入比 30 分钟写入贵。单看一次调用，这些选项只是几个勾；一个月跑下来，勾在哪边，账单会差出很大一截。

一次请求里面的步骤也会把账单推高。TechTarget 10 月 14 日的一篇行业稿提到，企业从单次问答转到多步智能体以后，一次业务请求会触发检索、对账、工具调用、重试和校验。推理模型的思考过程按更贵的输出计价。稿里给了一个说明性例子，不是某家公司的实测账单，单价降一半，流程用掉四倍 token，总成本仍会翻倍。这个算术不复杂，采购时却很容易只对比单价。

一篇题为 The Price Reversal Phenomenon 的预印本做了成对比较，12 项任务，8 个模型。32% 的情况下，标价更低的模型总推理费用反而更高。预印本没有经过同行评审，样本也有限，但它指出的问题很具体，单价低不等于这次任务便宜。TechTarget 那篇稿还提到，Uber 据报在 4 月就用完了全年 AI 预算。这是媒体报道，只能当作一个侧面参照，预算被消耗的速度和单价走势可以脱节。

所以看这轮降价，价目表只能当起点。实验室的真实成本、折扣和内部账，外面看不见。能看见的是报价、档位和计费规则。一次智能体任务要跑多少轮、缓存命中多少、重试几次、上下文有多长，这些数字才决定账单。价目表上的数字越来越接近，账单的差距反而可能拉大。

items.title: 【AIが実務案件の41.3%を完成？！ なのにAnthropicは「AIの開発能力」を意図的に制限？！】
items.summary:
【AIが実務案件の41.3%を完成？！ なのにAnthropicは「AIの開発能力」を意図的に制限？！】

昨日発表されたClaude Fable 5.2、今回かなり凄い！！

衝撃的なのは、単なる知能ランキングではなく、AIが「仕事を完成させる能力」。

Scale AIとCAISのRemote Labor Indexは、実際のフリーランス案件を使い、人間のプロと同等以上の納品品質に達したかを評価するもの。

結果は、

Claude Fable 5.2：41.30%
Claude Opus 5.5：21.25%
OpenAI GPT-6 Astra：20.83%

なんと次点のほぼ2倍！

240案件を収集し、正式ランキングは非公開230件で評価。もちろん「世の中の仕事の41%がなくなる」という意味ではないけど、これはかなり大きな進化だと思う。

じゃあ、米国トップ4社の競争はどうなっているのか？

Artificial Analysisの総合知能指数（最高クラスの推論設定）は、

Fable 5.2：65
Google Gemini 4 Carbon：60
Opus 5.5：59
GPT-6 Astra：57
GPT-6.1 Sol：55
Meta Muse Wonder Full：50

最高性能ではAnthropicが一歩リード。Googleも猛烈に巻き返してきた。

一方、OpenAIはSolをAstraの5分の1のAPI単価で提供し、難しい仕事と大量の普通の仕事でモデルを使い分ける戦略。

MetaもMuse Wonderで追い上げながら、WhatsApp、Instagram、Facebookという巨大Distributionを持っている。

ざっくり言えば、

Anthropic＝最高性能 × 難関タスク
Google＝モデル × インフラ × 業務自動化
OpenAI＝性能 × コスト効率 × エージェント実装
Meta＝エージェント × Distribution

という感じ。

ただ今回、一番面白いのはここから。

AnthropicはFable 5.2の学習段階で、AIが次世代AIを開発する一部の能力を、あえてOpus 5.5程度に抑えたと明かした。

GPUなどの処理を速くするカーネル最適化。より高性能なLLMを設計するアーキテクチャ改善。

つまり、AIがAIを進化させる能力。

公式説明は安全性のため。AIがAIを改良し、さらに強いAIが次のAIを作る。Recursive Self-Improvementが加速しすぎるリスクを抑えたいという考え方。

でも、ここで疑問。

この制限、本当に続けられるの？？

トップ企業は制限できても、追いかける会社がAIによるAI開発を全力で進めたら、どうなる？

他社も制限を外す圧力が強まる。完全に囚人のジレンマ。

しかもAnthropicは10月26日にIPOへ向けたS-1を提出済み。安全性のアピール、競合への技術流出防止という戦略的な意味も考えられる。ただし、ここは僕の推測で、実際の決定理由が公表されたわけではない。

そしてもう一つ重要なのが、前から言っている「ハーネス」。

LLMという頭脳が賢くても、仕事を分解して、ツールやデータを使い、複数のAIが協力し、失敗したらやり直し、成果物を検証しなければ仕事は完成しない。

これからは、

Intelligence × Harness × Tools × Data × Cost × Distribution

まで見ないとAIの実力は分からない。

しかもこれはAI企業だけの話ではない。

会社は「人間を組織するもの」から「人間とAIエージェントを組織するもの」へ。

最も強い企業は、社員数が一番多い企業ではなく、人間とAIを組み合わせて最も大きな成果を出せる企業になるかもしれない。

PS：しかし最近のAIの進化、追いかけるだけでも大変すぎる…w 😂

items.summary:
𝗥𝗘𝗦𝗘𝗔𝗥𝗖𝗛 𝗡𝗢𝗧𝗘 𝗢𝗡 𝗣𝗥𝗜𝗖𝗘 𝗔𝗡𝗗 𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗟𝗟𝗜𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗖𝗘 𝗥𝗔𝗡𝗞𝗜𝗡𝗚𝗦

𝗢𝗕𝗦𝗘𝗥𝗩𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

https://t.co/QPRInngWC8's October report contains an unusual dataset: model rankings built on what developers actually used and paid, not on vendor claims. Two of its four lenses, cost and intelligence, tell a more nuanced story than a single leaderboard would.

✓ Documented: The Price Ranking compares input, output and weighted prices. GPT 5 Nano tops both the weighted and input rankings from low to high, while Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT 6 Luna hold top five weighted positions and top four input positions.

✓ Documented: On output prices, MiMo V2.6 Flash, MiniMax M3.1 Flash, GLM 5.3 Flash and Qwen3.8 Flash hold the four lowest places. MiniMax is priced at USD 0.3 per million tokens, only USD 0.02 behind the leader, while GLM sits at USD 0.35 and Qwen at USD 0.376.

𝗘𝗩𝗜𝗗𝗘𝗡𝗖𝗘 & 𝗠𝗘𝗖𝗛𝗔𝗡𝗜𝗦𝗠

The pattern suggests specialization by billing phase. International models lead where input volume dominates, which the report connects to large knowledge bases, long document retrieval and general dialogue. Chinese models lead where output volume dominates, which the report connects to high concurrency generation.

Interpretation: price competition is no longer a single race. Which model is cheapest depends on whether a workload reads more than it writes, which is why a weighted ranking and separate input and output rankings are all needed.

✓ Documented: The Smart Ranking combines the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a frontier cost performance scatter plot. Kimi K3.1 Pro scored 55.1, in the top three globally behind Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5. Qwen3.8 Max scored 53.4, fifth globally.

Interpretation: lower price and higher intelligence are not opposites. Models near the top of intelligence and models near the bottom of output cost both appear in the same data.

𝗔𝗣𝗣𝗟𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 & 𝗘𝗖𝗢𝗦𝗬𝗦𝗧𝗘𝗠

The report concludes that platform developers have moved from single minded price comparison toward demand driven scheduling: a cost performance engine for high frequency concurrency and a high intelligence brain for complex reasoning. That is a design pattern, not just a ranking.

For builders in the TRON ecosystem, the practical implication is routing by workload. A pipeline can read with an input efficient model, generate with an output efficient model and reserve the highest ranked intelligence for the steps that need it, all behind one https://t.co/QPRInngWC8 key and balance.

The note also underlines why neutral infrastructure matters. A platform that carries many vendors can publish comparative evidence from its own traffic, and the TRON ecosystem benefits from that evidence being open.

As rankings keep updating with real usage, the TRON ecosystem will be able to steer its agents by data instead of reputation.

@justinsuntron @BAI_AGI #TRONEcoStar

items.title: AIPOCH Open-Science averaged 0.7467 on a local 25-task DiscoveryBench validation subset, testing how an agent turns real
items.summary:
AIPOCH Open-Science averaged 0.7467 on a local 25-task DiscoveryBench validation subset, testing how an agent turns real datasets into testable hypotheses.
All 25 tasks received scores: 18 received full credit, 5 received zero, and the remaining 2 received partial credit.

What does DiscoveryBench ask an agent to do?
Start with a natural-language research goal, real data and column descriptions. Inspect and clean the data, construct variables, run analyses, then return a hypothesis and the workflow used to produce it.

This evaluation focuses on data analysis and hypothesis construction, rather than literature retrieval or multiple-choice question answering.

The local setup used deepseek-v4-flash with default reasoning, plus a Specialist configured with seven skills covering hypothesis generation, exploratory analysis, statistics, critical evaluation and output handling. Tasks ran through a Python notebook using pandas, statsmodels and pyreadstat, with network access and package installation disabled during execution.

How scoring worked:
The report describes a local replication of the official five-step evaluation flow, retaining the official prompt text and using deepseek-v4-flash as the judge. Hypotheses are evaluated through their context, variables and relationships, with a formula producing the final score.

0.7467 is a mean evaluation score—not 74.67% answer accuracy or independent validation of scientific discoveries.

The accompanying reference chart also includes these official Test records:
- ReAct / openai/gpt-5.5-2026-04-23 — 0.3893
- ReAct / openai/gpt-5.4-2026-03-05 — 0.3776
- ReAct / google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview — 0.3707

These are context, not a head-to-head comparison. The local evaluation uses 25 validation tasks and a DeepSeek judge; official references use the full Test set and gpt-4-1106-preview. The local result has not been submitted to the official leaderboard.

The full chart preserves all 30 supplied official records, with the local result shown separately.
